row.notes: named from its log messages (channel CompressedSaveDataSerialiser): 'Received file read request, result is not ok '%s' | Received file read request results when we didn't expect them | File read request returned unexpected results'. w4r 2026-10-28 (decomp 0x14364c2de-0x14364c6b3): the whole profile decodes here, not in SAVE_DATA. Parent heap = Game_CompressedSave_GetTempHeaps()[[serialiser+8]+0 != 0 ? 0 : 1] (SAVE_TEMP_ALLOC 75M or SAVE_TEMP_ALLOC_HUGE 200M); its largest free block (heap vt+0x80(heap,1), the 'Largest' of Ne_ReportMemoryError) is allocated (vt+0x18) and made a pool named SAVE_PROPERTY_BAG_TEMP (Ne_Init_TempPool_Thunk); the root bag {pool, 0, 0} is filled by Ne_BagCodec_ReadBag (raw 0x14364c64f or through the decompressing stream 0x14568e190 at 0x14364c49c), handed to 0x14364c6f0 (root deserialise, .data1 0x150b11430), then Ne_Bag_Clear and Game_CompressedSave_FreeTempPool_Thunk free it all. Unclaimed root children are therefore freed with the pool at the end of the load.

verify.notes: V1479 Load overflow: the pool's allocator Ne_TempPool_Alloc reports error 0xc through Ne_TempPool_ReportError, which is fatal (Ne_FatalAbort) when pool+0x80 bit 0 is set. That bit is serialiser+0x512 (pool name block +0x20 at 0x14364c55x; the init copies it at .data1 0x151e53ac8), and the profile's save jobs set it to 1 (Game_CompressedSave_Construct_Thunk notes). So a profile load that outgrows the largest free block is fatal heap error 0xc; the 25 MB mid-session builder 0x14365a320 passes 0 and only gets 0xc back.
V6101 name/log string and function size match the code; strings verified via cstr (no direct call site; vtable/indirect)
